name: Manathunainathar Temple, Tiruvalivalam
deity: Shiva as Manathunainathar (Hrudaya Kamala Nathar, the companion of the heart), with the goddess Maazhai Onkanni (Madhyayadhakshi)
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Valivalam, near Tiruvarur, honours Shiva as Manathunainathar — the companion of the heart — with the goddess Maazhai Onkanni. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by all three great saints, Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar, its very name promises a lord who stands beside the devotee in the depths of the mind.

sections.history: Valivalam lies about 18–19 km from Tiruvarur, near Tirukaravasal, in Nagapattinam district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by all three of the great saints — Tirugnana Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later; the lord here is Manathunainathar, also called Hrudaya Kamala Nathar, 'lord of the lotus of the heart.'
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Manathunainathar in the sanctum, with the goddess Maazhai Onkanni — also called Madhyayadhakshi and Valaiyangkanni — in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The sthala vriksham is the punnai (laurel), and the sacred tank is the Sankara (Chakkara) Theertham.
sections.legends: The lord's names carry the shrine's whole meaning: Manathunainathar is 'the lord who is the companion of the mind,' and Hrudaya Kamala Nathar 'the lord of the heart's lotus' — the Shiva who dwells within and stands beside the devotee in every trouble of the heart. That all three Tevaram saints sang here marks the place as dear to the Shaiva tradition. The fuller sthala purana, as with many delta shrines, is carried chiefly in the Tevaram verses and local memory.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail near Tiruvarur include Valivalam among their stops.
sections.experience: At Valivalam the pilgrim comes to the lord who is the heart's own companion. Before Manathunainathar and Maazhai Onkanni, the visitor brings the burdens of the mind to a Tevaram temple sung by all three saints, and feels the nearness of a Shiva who steadies the heart from within.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Valivalam is about 18–19 km from Tiruvarur, near Tirukaravasal, in Nagapattinam district. Tiruvarur and Nagapattinam are the nearest rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village.
